units.title: A Distance That's Just Right
units.sub: A little closer and we'd be Venus; a little farther and we'd be Mars. Earth sits in exactly the right place.

share.v: who established it and didn’t create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited

blocks.h: The surface of Venus is hotter than 460°C, hot enough to melt lead. On Mars the air pressure is less than one percent of Earth's, so liquid water can hardly survive on the surface. Tucked between the two, Earth averages about 15°C, and rivers, lakes and seas flow everywhere.
For Yahweh who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it, who established it and didn’t create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited says: “I am Yahweh. There is no other.
The habitable zone

Astronomers call the range of distances around a star where a planet's surface could hold liquid water the “habitable zone.” For our Sun, this range is estimated to begin at about 0.95 astronomical units, with the outer edge estimated at somewhere between 1.4 and 1.7 astronomical units, depending on the model. Earth sits at 1 astronomical unit, about 150 million kilometers from the Sun.
It's like warming yourself around a campfire: too close and you get scorched, too far and you freeze. Earth sits in the spot that is just warm enough, and it stays there all year round.
A nearly circular orbit

Earth's orbit around the Sun is very nearly a perfect circle, with an eccentricity of only about 0.017. If the orbit were stretched out flat like those of many exoplanets, each year would swing wildly between scorching heat and bitter cold.

The Sun itself is also remarkably steady. It is a stable, middle-aged star, and over one solar cycle its brightness varies by only about one part in a thousand, unlike many stars that erupt in violent flares.
Distance isn't the only requirement. Earth also needs the right amount of atmosphere and greenhouse effect: with no greenhouse gases at all, the average surface temperature would drop to about −18°C.

The boundaries of the habitable zone are still being studied, and they depend on atmospheric composition, cloud cover and planetary mass. Astronomers have discovered thousands of exoplanets, but none has yet been confirmed to have all of these Earth-like conditions at once.
The surface temperature of Venus is above about 460°C; the surface air pressure on Mars is less than one percent of Earth's.
Earth's orbital eccentricity is about 0.017, close to a perfect circle.
The Sun's habitable zone begins at about 0.95 astronomical units, with the outer edge estimated at 1.4 to 1.7 astronomical units, depending on the model.
That Earth meets so many conditions for habitability at once points to a God who made the earth “to be inhabited.” This is an inference of faith.
His goodness: a home prepared for us
Isaiah says God “didn’t create it a waste,” but “formed it to be inhabited.” Earth isn't a landing spot we stumbled onto by chance. It is a home a loving Father prepared for His children.
The heavens are the heavens of Yahweh; but he has given the earth to the children of men.
He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.
In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you.
The God who prepared the earth for us has also prepared an eternal home for us in Jesus Christ.
Look out the window: there is air, there is water, there is just the right temperature. All the things we have every day and never think about are God's grace.
Reflect: What are three things you take for granted today that are actually gifts from God?
Prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for preparing this home for me. Help me stop taking Your grace for granted, and to offer You thanks every day. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Give thanks in everything: count your blessings one by one, and the glory goes to God.
Return to our proper place: it isn't that we adapted to the earth; God prepared the earth for us.
Build your relationship with God first: knowing the One who prepared it all matters more than enjoying what He prepared.

units.title: The Gift of the Moon
units.sub: The moon doesn't just light up the night sky. It steadies Earth's tilt and drives the ocean tides.

share.v: He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set.

blocks.h: Compared with its planet, our moon is unusually large: its diameter is about a quarter of Earth's. This big moon is like a hand steadying a spinning top, keeping Earth's axis from wobbling wildly.
God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.
Stable seasons

Earth's axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees, which gives us spring, summer, autumn and winter. Over long periods, this angle only drifts slowly between about 22 and 24.5 degrees. Calculations by French astronomer Jacques Laskar show that the moon's gravity is a major reason Earth's axis stays stable.
Mars, which has no large moon, has seen its axial tilt swing dramatically over long periods, possibly anywhere from near 0 degrees to more than 60 degrees, with its climate lurching along with it.
Picture a spinning top with someone gently holding it steady. It spins smoothly. The moon is that steadying hand on the earth.
The heartbeat of the ocean

The moon's gravity causes the tides, with about twice the tidal effect of the Sun. Every day, high and low tides stir the seawater, making the coastal intertidal zone one of the richest places for life.
Some research suggests that even without the moon, the changes in Earth's axis might be milder than early estimates. Just how much the moon contributes to axial stability is still being discussed.
Earth's axial tilt is about 23.4 degrees and varies over long periods between about 22 and 24.5 degrees.
The moon contributes significantly to the long-term stability of Earth's tilt; studies differ on how much it would vary without the moon.
The axial tilt of Mars shows large, chaotic variations over long periods.
The moon's tidal effect is about twice that of the Sun.
He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set.
His faithfulness: steady seasons
Farmers can sow and harvest on time because the seasons are stable. Behind those stable seasons is a moon placed just right, and the One who placed the moon is the faithful God.
It will be established forever like the moon, the faithful witness in the sky.” Selah.
Psalm 89 uses the moon as a witness to God's covenant with David. The moon rises day after day like a witness in the sky, reminding us that God's promises never change.
Look at the moon tonight. It gives off no light of its own, yet it reflects the light of the Sun and lights up the dark.
Reflect: Am I like the moon, reflecting the light of Christ, or am I trying to shine on my own?
Prayer: Lord, You are the One who holds my life steady. When my life wobbles, hold me up, so that I can stand firm in You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Selflessness: the moon doesn't give off its own light; it only reflects the Sun. It is no longer I, but Christ who lives in me.
Let Jesus receive the glory: when people see something good in me, let them see that Jesus is the source of the light.
Become a spiritual companion: just as the moon steadies the earth, I can be a steady presence in someone else's life.

quiz.e: The moon is much closer than the Sun, so its tidal effect is about twice as strong.

units.title: Wonderful Water
units.sub: The most ordinary substance, with the most extraordinary properties.

share.v: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.

blocks.h: When almost any substance turns from liquid to solid, it shrinks, gets denser and sinks. Water does the opposite: ice is lighter than water and floats on top.

If ice sank, lakes and oceans would freeze from the bottom up, layer by layer, and many water creatures could not survive the winter. Because ice floats, it acts like a blanket over the water below, protecting the life within.
In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
A few unusual things about water

items: Ice is lighter than water: ice has a density of about 0.917 grams per cubic centimeter, about nine percent less than liquid water; water is densest at 4°C.
Very high specific heat: water can absorb or release a great deal of heat while its temperature changes only a little. This makes the oceans Earth's thermostat and keeps our body temperature steady.
Evaporation absorbs a lot of heat: that's why sweating cools us so well.
It dissolves many substances: nutrients, salts and oxygen all rely on water to carry them through our bodies and the soil.
Surface tension and capillary action: these help water climb from a tree's roots to treetops 100 meters high.

blocks.h: Water molecules are like people holding hands (hydrogen bonds), holding on not too tightly and not too loosely. It's this just-right “hand-holding” that gives water so many wonderful properties.

In 1913, Harvard physiological chemist Lawrence Henderson published The Fitness of the Environment, carefully listing the many ways water is “fit” for life, and arguing that the environment itself seems to have been prepared for life.
More recent research has found that water isn't just a passive background inside cells. It actively takes part in life processes such as protein folding and molecular recognition.
Ice is less dense than liquid water, and water is densest at about 4°C.
Water's specific heat and heat of vaporization are exceptionally high among common liquids.
Water actively takes part in biochemical processes in cells; the detailed mechanisms are still being studied.
That so many of water's properties benefit life at once points to purposeful design. This is a philosophical argument that goes back to Henderson.
His wisdom: wonder hidden in the ordinary
God often hides His deepest wisdom in the most ordinary things. We drink a glass of water every day, yet few people know how wonderful it is.
As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.
Our bodies can't live without water, and our souls can't live without God. At a well, Jesus said to a Samaritan woman:
but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.
He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, from within him will flow rivers of living water.
Pour a glass of water and drink it slowly. Thank God for this wonderful gift.
Reflect: Has my soul been dry lately, or refreshed by living water?
Prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the spring of living water. Satisfy the thirst in my heart, and let living water flow out from me to refresh others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Holy Spirit is my guide: the rivers of living water refer to the Holy Spirit (John 7:39). Ask to be filled with the Spirit every day.
Receive with your heart, relying on the Spirit: don't just understand with your head; receive with your heart.
Multiplication: living water is meant to flow out. Share what you received today with one person.

It makes the lake freeze faster
quiz.e: Lakes freeze from the top, and the water below stays liquid.

o: It keeps the oceans and our body temperature stable

quiz.e: “But he said this about the Spirit, which those believing in him were to receive.” (John 7:39)

units.title: The Invisible Shield
units.sub: The magnetic field, the atmosphere and the ozone layer protect life on earth day and night.

share.v: He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.

blocks.h: The Sun constantly blasts out charged particles, called the “solar wind,” at hundreds of kilometers per second. Around Earth is an invisible magnetic field that keeps most of the solar wind out.

The northern and southern lights are what happens when a few particles slip in along magnetic field lines into the high atmosphere over the poles and glow as they strike the air. The beautiful curtain of light you see is actually the shield at work.
He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
Three layers of protection

items: Magnetic field: generated by flowing liquid iron in Earth's outer core, it blocks most of the solar wind and cosmic rays.
Atmosphere: about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen; most meteors burn up in it before reaching the ground.
Ozone layer: located in the stratosphere, it absorbs most harmful ultraviolet B and almost all ultraviolet C.

blocks.h: Mars lost its global magnetic field long ago. NASA's MAVEN mission found that much of Mars' atmosphere has been stripped away into space by the solar wind.
Earth is like a spaceship surrounded by intense radiation and particle storms. The magnetic field is the hull, the atmosphere is the airtight cabin, and the ozone layer is the UV-blocking glass.
The ozone layer on the mend

In the late twentieth century, man-made chlorofluorocarbons damaged the ozone layer, and an “ozone hole” appeared over Antarctica. In 1987 nations signed the Montreal Protocol to phase out these substances. The World Meteorological Organization's 2022 assessment found that the ozone layer is gradually recovering, and over Antarctica it is expected to return to 1980 levels around 2066.
Earth's magnetic field is generated by flowing liquid metal in the outer core and deflects most of the solar wind.
The ozone layer absorbs most ultraviolet B and almost all ultraviolet C.
After losing its global magnetic field, Mars had much of its atmosphere stripped away by the solar wind; how much was lost, and over what time, is still being studied.
Since the Montreal Protocol, the ozone layer has been gradually recovering.
He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.
His goodness: protection that never stops
The magnetic field never rests, and the ozone layer never takes a day off. God's protection is like that: even while we sleep, He keeps watch over us.
Yahweh is your keeper. Yahweh is your shade on your right hand. The sun will not harm you by day, nor the moon by night.
It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in,
Think back over the past year. What dangers did you only find out about afterward? God's protection is often invisible.
Reflect: What have I been afraid of lately? Place it “in the shadow of the Almighty.”
Prayer: Lord, my protector, thank You for surrounding me with an invisible shield. I will no longer try to fend off everything on my own; I take refuge under Your wings. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: I don't have to be my own shield. Let the Lord take charge and protect me.
The responsibility of a steward: humanity once damaged the ozone layer, and humanity worked together to repair it. God has entrusted us to keep watch over this earth.
Comrades in arms: stand watch in prayer for your family and your brothers and sisters, and become a protection for one another.

quiz.q: What causes the northern and southern lights?
o: Charged particles striking the upper atmosphere and glowing
quiz.e: Particles enter the polar regions along magnetic field lines and glow as they strike the atmosphere.

units.title: The Breathing Earth
units.sub: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen; we take in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide.

share.v: he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things.

blocks.h: Some of the oxygen molecules in the breath you just took may have come from invisible phytoplankton in the ocean. About half of all photosynthesis on Earth takes place in the sea.
in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
A global exchange

Plants, algae and some bacteria use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugars, releasing oxygen. Animals and people breathe in oxygen, break down sugars for energy, and breathe out carbon dioxide. Back and forth, the two form the carbon and oxygen cycle.
It's like two neighbors trading things over the fence every day: you give me what I need, I give you what you need, and nobody owes anybody.
The most abundant protein on earth
The enzyme that “grabs” carbon dioxide is called Rubisco, and it may well be the most abundant protein on Earth.
Carbon dioxide makes up only about four parts in ten thousand of the atmosphere, yet that is enough to supply every plant on earth, and it also helps maintain the surface temperature.

Photosynthesis is a precise chain of steps: capturing photons, splitting water molecules, passing electrons along and building energy molecules. Its efficiency and regulation are still a hot topic of research.
About half of global primary production (photosynthesis) takes place in the ocean.
Rubisco is one of the most abundant proteins on Earth; estimates of its total global amount remain uncertain.
Carbon dioxide makes up about four parts in ten thousand of the atmosphere (about 420 ppm).
Plants and animals supply each other's needs, forming a mutually supporting system that points to a wise Designer.
He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things.
His goodness: every breath is grace
We breathe more than 20,000 times a day, yet we hardly ever think about it. Every breath is given freely by God through a wonderful cycle.
Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit!
At creation, God breathed into man and he became a living being. The risen Jesus breathed on His disciples, and they received the Holy Spirit and became new creations.
Quietly take five deep breaths. Each time you breathe in, say “Lord,” and each time you breathe out, say “thank You.”
Reflect: If every breath is a gift from God, what words will I speak with this breath?
Prayer: God who gives the breath of life, thank You for every breath. May my mouth open to praise You, and may I use the breath You give to bless others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Deny yourself: plants give their oxygen away to others. Live for Jesus and for others, not for yourself.
The order of relationships: first a living exchange with God, then a living exchange with people.
Let everything that has breath praise Yah (Psalm 150:6).

blocks.h: This week: put a plant at home or on your desk, and every time you see it, pray for someone.
Quiz

quiz.q: About how much of Earth's photosynthesis takes place in the ocean?
quiz.e: Phytoplankton in the ocean contribute about half of primary production.

quiz.q: Photosynthesis turns which two things into sugars?
quiz.e: And it releases oxygen.

quiz.e: John 20:22.

units.title: The Journey of Water
units.sub: From ocean to cloud, from rain to river, a single drop of water travels the whole world.

share.v: For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud,

blocks.h: Every year the Sun evaporates about 500,000 cubic kilometers of water from the oceans and land. It rises into the sky and falls again as rain and snow. A water molecule stays in the atmosphere for only about nine days on average before returning to the ground.
All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.
A cycle that never stops

items: Evaporation: sunlight warms the sea surface, and water rises as vapor, leaving the salt behind in the sea.
Condensation: the vapor cools high in the sky and condenses into clouds.
Precipitation: water droplets in the clouds grow larger and fall as rain or snow.
Runoff and infiltration: water flows into rivers, soaks into the ground, and eventually returns to the sea.

blocks.h: The Sun is like a giant water-purification plant, distilling salty seawater into fresh water every day and delivering it free of charge to the mountains, the fields and your kitchen tap.
Precious fresh water

About 97% of Earth's water is in the oceans. Fresh water makes up only about 2.5%, and most of that is frozen in glaciers and ice caps. The fresh water in rivers and lakes that we can use directly is a tiny fraction of the total, yet the water cycle keeps renewing it without end.

Some three thousand years ago, the book of Job already described it: “For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor, which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.” (Job 36:27–28)
Global evaporation totals about 500,000 cubic kilometers per year.
The average residence time of a water molecule in the atmosphere is about eight to ten days.
About 97% of Earth's water is seawater; fresh water is about 2.5%, and most of it is ice.
A self-renewing water-purification system displays the faithfulness and provision of the Creator.

For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater; so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
His faithfulness: His word never fails
When rain falls, it always produces results. God uses the water cycle as a picture: His word is the same. Once spoken, it will surely be fulfilled.
For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor, which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.
The next time it rains, don't just think of the inconvenience. Remember that God is watering the earth once again.
Reflect: What word has God spoken to me that I am still waiting to see fulfilled?
Prayer: Faithful God, Your word never returns to You void. I believe that what You have spoken over my life will be fulfilled. Water my dry heart like the rain. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: God's word is like rain; receive it every day, and your life will bud and bear fruit.
The eight steps of changing our mindset: information, revelation, conviction, practice, review, correction, repetition, multiplication. Let the word keep cycling through your life.
Multiplication: what I have received must flow out to water others.

blocks.h: This week: memorize Isaiah 55:11 and write it out for a friend who is waiting on God.
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the main source of energy that drives the water cycle?
quiz.e: Sunlight warms the sea surface, causing water to evaporate and rise.

quiz.q: About how much of Earth's water is fresh water?
quiz.e: About 97% is seawater; fresh water is only about 2.5%.

quiz.q: In Isaiah 55, what do the rain and snow picture?
o: God's word, which will not return void
quiz.e: “So is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void.”

units.title: The Living Ground
units.sub: From the tectonic plates deep below to the soil beneath our feet, the earth is always moving and always nurturing life.

share.v: What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word, and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit, and brings forth, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.

blocks.h: A small pinch of healthy soil is home to hundreds of millions of microbes, more than the number of people on earth. Quietly they break down fallen leaves and return nutrients to the plants.
As for the earth, out of it comes bread. Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire. Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.
A crust that moves

Earth's outer shell is divided into many plates that move slowly. Earth is the only planet known to have active plate tectonics. Plate movement builds mountains and forms mineral deposits, and it carries carbonates from the seafloor back into Earth's interior, where volcanoes later release carbon dioxide.
This “carbonate–silicate cycle” works like a long-term thermostat: when Earth warms, rock weathering speeds up and absorbs more carbon dioxide; when it cools, weathering slows down.
It's like the thermostat on an air conditioner: when it's too hot, it cools harder; when it's too cold, it eases off, keeping the room comfortable.
Life beneath our feet

Soil isn't just dirt and sand. It is a living system made of rock fragments, organic matter, water, air and countless living things. A single gram of soil may hold thousands of different kinds of microbes.
The vast majority of soil microbial diversity has not yet been named or studied, and it has been called one of biology's “final frontiers.”
Earth is the only planet currently known to have active plate tectonics.
The carbonate–silicate cycle helps stabilize Earth's long-term temperature; its strength and time scale are still being studied.
Soil contains extremely rich microbial communities, most of which have not yet been studied.
The earth's regulating and life-nurturing functions display a God who makes the land bring forth its produce and provides for every living thing.
You visit the earth, and water it. You greatly enrich it.
His wisdom: the unseen workers
No one sees the microbes in the soil, yet they feed the whole earth. God, too, often uses unseen people and unseen things to accomplish great things.
When Jesus told the parable of the sower, the focus wasn't the seed, but the soil:
What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word, and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit, and brings forth, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.
If you can, go outside and touch the soil. That is a place where God is at work every day.
Reflect: Is my heart like the roadside, the rocky ground, the thorns, or the good soil?
Prayer: Lord, break up the hard ground of my heart. Remove the stones and thorns, and make me good soil, so that Your word may bear a hundredfold fruit in me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility: “humility” and “humus” (soil) share the same root. A humble heart is good soil.
Life first, then relationships, then ministry: fruit grows out of good soil. When our life is healthy, ministry naturally bears fruit.
Serve quietly: like the microbes in the soil, don't seek to be seen; seek only to nourish others.

blocks.h: This week: do one act of service that nobody knows about, seen only by your Father in heaven (Matthew 6:4).
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the only planet currently known to have active plate tectonics?
quiz.e: Plate tectonics helps regulate Earth's long-term temperature.

quiz.q: In the parable of the sower, which soil produces a hundredfold?
quiz.e: “What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word, and understands it.”

quiz.q: What work do the microbes in the soil do?
o: Break down organic matter and return nutrients to plants
quiz.e: They are the earth's unseen workers.

units.title: The Earth Is Yahweh's
units.sub: The earth is full of God's riches. God has entrusted it to us, to cultivate it and keep it.

share.v: The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.

blocks.h: Scientists estimate that there may be about 8.7 million species of eukaryotic life on Earth, yet only about 1.2 million have been formally named so far. In other words, most of the creatures God made, we have yet to meet.
Yahweh, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.
An interconnected web

Bees pollinate flowers, and flowers feed the bees; forests hold the soil and water in place, and rivers nourish the forests. Every living thing in an ecosystem is connected to others. Lose one link, and the whole web is affected.
It's like a tightly woven net: cut one thread and it seems like nothing, but cut too many and the whole net falls apart.
Our place in it all

Human beings are the only creatures able to study, understand and consciously care for the whole earth. We can destroy, and we can also restore. The worldwide effort to repair the ozone layer is one example.
The Bible gives humanity the role not of owner, but of steward: the earth belongs to God, we are entrusted to manage it, and one day we will give an account to Him.
There are about 8.7 million species of eukaryotes on Earth (an estimate), of which about 1.2 million have been named.
Species in an ecosystem depend on one another, for example through pollination and food webs.
Humans are entrusted stewards, not owners. This is the biblical worldview.
The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.
His righteousness and goodness: entrusting and caring
Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
God placing the world into human hands is an act of trust in us, and also a calling for us.
See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
For the creation waits with eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed.
All creation is waiting for God's children to be revealed. When we live out the life of Christ, even the earth benefits along with us.
Look at a tree, a bird or a flower near you. They all belong to God, and God cares for them. How much more does He care for you.
Reflect: What has God entrusted to me to manage? My time, money, body, family, and this earth.

Prayer: Lord of all, everything is Yours. Make me a faithful steward who takes good care of all You have entrusted to me, so that one day You will say to me, “Well done, good and faithful servant.” In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: the earth is Yahweh's, and everything I have is His too.
Build God's kingdom system: within whatever I am responsible for, govern according to God's heart, so that His will is done on earth.
People matter more than things: we manage creation to bless people, not to possess things.

blocks.h: This week: choose one concrete way to care for creation, such as cutting down on waste or picking up litter, and invite a friend to do it with you.
Congratulations on completing the Earth Hall! From a distance that is just right to an earth entrusted to us, you have seen a God who prepared a home for us and watches over it day and night.
Quiz

quiz.e: Only about 1.2 million of them have been named.

quiz.q: According to Genesis 2:15, why did God put the man in the garden of Eden?
quiz.e: Humans are entrusted stewards.

quiz.q: According to Psalm 24:1, to whom do the earth and its fullness belong?
quiz.e: “The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness…”

units.title: Plates and Volcanoes: The Moving Crust
units.sub: The summit of Mount Everest was once seafloor, and the island of Taiwan is still being squeezed. The ground beneath your feet has never stopped moving.

share.v: For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed, but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,”says Yahweh who has mercy on you.

blocks.h: The highest rock in the world was once seafloor. The rock layers at the summit of Everest are fossil-bearing marine limestone, so when climbers stand on top of the Earth, they are standing on an ancient sea bed.
If you live in Taiwan, this is even closer to home: the distance between Lanyu (Orchid Island) and Penghu shrinks by about 8 centimeters every year. This island is still being squeezed.
The mountains rose, the valleys sank down, to the place which you had assigned to them.
An idea that waited half a century

In 1912 the 32-year-old German meteorologist Alfred Wegener published his idea of continental drift, arguing that the continents had once been joined together. The scientific community responded coolly, mainly because he could not say what force could push whole continents. In 1930 he died on an expedition across the Greenland ice sheet, and never saw his idea vindicated.

The turning point came from the seafloor. During the Second World War, Harry Hess, a Princeton geologist who was the captain of a US Navy transport ship, used his voyages across the Pacific to survey the seafloor. In 1962 he published “History of Ocean Basins,” proposing that new seafloor is created at mid-ocean ridges and pushed outward to both sides. In 1963 Vine and Matthews used magnetic stripes in seafloor rock to provide the first key test.

The seafloor is like a tape slowly being fed out from the middle. When magma cools, its magnetic minerals record the direction of the Earth’s magnetic field at that time; when the field reverses, the next stretch is recorded in the opposite direction. So stripes appear, symmetrical on both sides of the mid-ocean ridge, and let us rewind the tape and read the history of the seafloor.
How slow, and how big

The US Geological Survey’s comparison is that plates move at about the speed fingernails grow. That is so slow you never feel it in a lifetime, yet accumulated over millions of years it is enough to push up mountains and open and close oceans.

Taiwan sits right on the front line of this collision. GPS measures Lanyu moving relative to Penghu at about 81.5 millimeters per year; researchers describe Taiwan as the product of the Luzon volcanic arc colliding with the margin of continental China, a collision that is still going on. The Huatung (East Rift) Valley is the suture zone.
Earth’s long-term thermostat

In 1981 Walker, Hays and Kasting proposed a negative feedback: when the climate warms, the weathering of silicate rocks speeds up and removes more carbon dioxide; when it cools, weathering slows down. The authors themselves explained that the numerical details remain speculative, and that this mechanism can partly stabilize surface temperature. Carbonates deposited on the seafloor are subducted with the plates, and some of that carbon returns to the atmosphere through volcanoes, so volcanoes are also part of this ledger.

Think of it as a household account book: volcanoes keep making deposits, and weathering and sedimentation make the withdrawals. The hotter the weather, the faster the withdrawals; the colder the weather, the slower. Plate motion lets money that has been stored on the seafloor have a chance to return to circulation.

Venus is the neighbor often used for comparison: its surface is about 740 K (about 465 degrees Celsius) with a pressure of about 92 bar, and it has no global plate network. Whether it once had oceans is still unsettled; both scenarios have their advocates, and the key data are missing.
Are plates a necessary condition for habitability?

People often say, “No plates, no life,” but that is overstated. Some models show that “stagnant lid” planets without plate motion could, under the right conditions, also sustain a habitable climate for about 1 to 5 billion years; but those results rest on explicit premises, such as the total amount of carbon dioxide falling within a certain range, and the model authors also caution that the uncertainties are large.

items.n: Plate motion matters for long-term habitability
items.h: Earth’s carbon cycle and climate regulation actually work through plate tectonics, and this is the only case we know has life; the contrast with Venus is also thought-provoking.

items.n: Plate motion is not necessarily required
items.h: Models show that stagnant-lid planets can also maintain climate through volcanism and weathering; with only one sample, we cannot turn “Earth is like this” into “it must be like this.”

blocks.h: On the same topic, different claims do not have the same degree of certainty.

Earth’s lithosphere is divided into a number of plates that are continuously moving, at speeds that GPS can measure directly; the Geological Survey’s popular comparison is that it is about the speed fingernails grow.

Taiwan lies in an active collision zone, and the GPS velocity of Lanyu relative to Penghu is about 81.5 millimeters per year; the Central Weather Administration also describes the Philippine Sea Plate’s motion as about 8 centimeters per year.

The rock layers at the summit of Everest are fossil-bearing marine limestone. Their age is generally thought to be early to middle Ordovician, but the summit samples this rests on are few, and researchers say more sampling is needed.
The carbonate-silicate cycle has a stabilizing effect on Earth’s long-term temperature; its strength, its timescale and how it worked on the early Earth are still being studied.
Whether plate motion is a necessary condition for planetary habitability has no settled answer; model studies suggest it may not be.

An Earth that moves and regulates itself is a fitting occasion to marvel at the Creator’s wisdom and goodness. This is an interpretation of faith, not a scientific conclusion. The same motion also brings earthquakes and volcanic disasters, a heavy question we face squarely in Unit 12.
The earth moves; His covenant does not

Psalm 104 is a poem, praising the Creator with pictures of waters fleeing and mountains rising. “That it should not be moved forever” speaks of God upholding the earth so that people can dwell on it securely; it is not a geological report. Many evangelical interpreters read passages like this as poetic language, and so there is no need to quarrel with GPS data.
He laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be moved forever. You covered it with the deep as with a cloak. The waters stood above the mountains.
Interestingly, the Bible itself frankly admits that mountains move. The prophet says the mountains may depart, and then points us to what truly does not move:
For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed, but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,”says Yahweh who has mercy on you.

This covenant that is not removed finally stood on a small hill. At the moment Jesus breathed His last, the Gospel records the earth’s response; on the morning of His resurrection, the earth shook once more. Human sin and death were shaken, and what opened to us is a kingdom that can never be shaken.
Behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
Therefore, receiving a Kingdom that can’t be shaken, let’s have grace, through which we serve God acceptably, with reverence and awe,

Look at your fingernails. The little bit that has grown since last week is about the distance the crust beneath your feet has moved in the same time. You are sitting right now on a piece of ground moving quietly forward, and the Lord who holds it all up has never dozed off.
Meditate: What am I building my sense of security on right now? My work, my savings, my health, or the words of Jesus? If that ground moved, could I still stand?

Pray: Lord who laid the foundations of the earth, my life often shakes and I am often afraid. Thank You that Your loving kindness does not depart from me, and thank You that Jesus has opened to me the kingdom that cannot be shaken. Rebuild my life on Your words. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: Jesus said the one who hears and does builds his house on the rock. This week choose one word of the Lord and really do it.

Letting God be God and people be people: people can measure how many centimeters a plate moves each year, but cannot stop it by even one centimeter. Admitting our limits is what lets us hand tomorrow to God in peace.
People matter more than tasks: if you live in an earthquake zone, everyday care is the most practical preparation; remember the people near you who live alone or have difficulty moving.

blocks.h: This week: Spend fifteen minutes with your family checking your emergency go-bag and agreeing on a meeting point after an earthquake; then check in on an older person who lives alone and ask whether their home needs help securing the cabinets.
Pass it on: In your life, what is there that could not be shaken away even if heaven and earth shook?
Quick quiz

quiz.q: What was the main reason Wegener’s continental drift theory was not accepted at the time?
o: He could not say what force could push the continents
quiz.e: The evidence he observed was strong but lacked a driving mechanism; later research on seafloor spreading filled in that piece.

quiz.q: What is the more honest way to put the statement “without plate motion, life would be impossible”?
o: Still unsettled, and some models show it may not be necessary
quiz.e: Earth’s climate regulation is indeed tied to plates, but with only one sample, models of stagnant-lid planets show other possibilities.

quiz.q: According to Isaiah 54:10, even if the mountains are removed, what will not depart from us?
quiz.e: Mountains may move, but God’s loving kindness and covenant of peace are not removed.

units.title: The Deep Sea: A Wonder No One Sees
units.sub: Humans have seen with their own eyes only about one hundred-thousandth of the deep seafloor. All the rest has gone on living just fine.

share.v: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?

blocks.h: Piece together all the deep seafloor humans have seen with their own eyes in seventy years, and it would be only about one tenth the size of Belgium.

In proportion, that is less than 0.001%. In a book of a hundred thousand pages, we have read less than one page, and mostly the same few pages from one corner. Everywhere else, right now, things are glowing, feeding and multiplying, and they have never waited for us.
“Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?
What does “explored” actually mean?

The ocean covers more than 70% of the Earth’s surface, with an average depth of about 3,682 meters; Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 10,935 meters. Put Mount Everest in it and the summit would still be two kilometers below the surface.

You may have heard that “humans have explored only 5% of the ocean.” Numbers like this get forwarded a lot, but seldom is it made clear what “explored” means. A more reliable account has to separate things: as of April 2026, about 28.7% of the global seafloor has been mapped with modern high-resolution sonar; the deep seafloor (below 200 meters) that has actually been seen with eyes or cameras was estimated in 2025 at less than 0.001%, and even if the estimate were off by a factor of ten, it would still be under 0.01%.

Sonar mapping is like drawing the street map of a city from an airplane; seeing it with your own eyes is like actually walking into one of the houses. We have rough street sketches of about thirty percent, but the houses we have entered are pitifully few, and almost all of them are in the same neighborhood.
1977: a boatload of geologists ran into a city

In February 1977, at the Galápagos Rift, at a depth of about 2,500 meters, the submersible Alvin made its dive number 713, carrying the pilot Donnelly and the scientists Jack Corliss and Tjeerd van Andel. They had come to look for hydrothermal vents on the seafloor. They thought there would be no life there, and did not bring a single biologist aboard the ship.

What they saw were clams, mussels, crabs, octopuses and red-tipped tube worms packed together around the vents. The surrounding water was only about 2 degrees Celsius, while the water near the vent openings was much warmer. They did not have enough formaldehyde for the specimens they brought up, so they preserved them with Russian vodka they had bought in Panama.
A food chain that does not begin with sunlight

Almost every food chain on land begins with photosynthesis. Here the starting point is bacteria: they use the hydrogen sulfide in the vent water to make nutrients, and the other animals live on them. In 1981 Colleen Cavanaugh and colleagues reported in the journal Science that cells inside the giant tube worms were probably chemoautotrophic symbionts of just this kind.

A whole city has a blackout, yet one neighborhood is brightly lit, because every household there has its own small generator. The ecosystem of a deep-sea vent is a neighborhood that is not connected to the main grid of sunlight.
Three quarters of the creatures in the dark glow

Séverine Martini and Steven Haddock of the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute went through 17 years of remotely operated vehicle footage, from the surface down to about 3,900 meters, and classified more than 350,000 animals. They found that about 76% were capable of bioluminescence, and that this proportion stayed fairly stable with depth.
The study site was off California and cannot be taken as equal to the global ocean. But in this stretch of sea, glowing is the norm.

In 2025 Peng and colleagues published in Nature on chemosynthetic communities at the very bottom of the trenches, and the word in their title is “flourishing.” The more humans look down, the harder it becomes to think of the deep sea as a desert.

Katherine Bell’s team also pointed out a blind spot: more than 65% of known visual records of the deep sea are concentrated in the waters off the United States, Japan and New Zealand, and nearly thirty percent are low-resolution images from before 1980; of the records of about 44,000 dives, 97% come from five countries. Our impression of the deep sea is really the impression from a few windows.
Let us separate the claims and mark how certain each one is.
The ocean covers more than 70% of the Earth’s surface and holds about 97% of the Earth’s water; the average depth is about 3,682 meters and Challenger Deep about 10,935 meters.
In 1977 Alvin discovered a hydrothermal vent community at the Galápagos Rift, and its food chain begins with bacteria that use hydrogen sulfide.

Humans have seen with their own eyes less than 0.001% of the deep seafloor. This is a 2025 estimate based on publicly available dive records, and the authors themselves mark their range of uncertainty; there may be unpublished military or commercial data that were not counted.
About 76% of animal individuals off California can emit light. The measurement itself is solid, but whether it can be extrapolated to the global ocean needs more data.

That the deep sea was rich long before humans saw it fits what the Bible says, “God saw that it was good”: the value of created things does not depend on a human audience. This is an interpretation of faith; science neither proves nor denies it.
Perspectives Room
How should we understand a beauty that no one sees?

items.h: Glowing is for hunting, courting and hiding, and vent animals are what natural selection achieved in an extreme environment. “Beauty” is something humans project onto it afterward, and the deep sea itself does not care. This explanation is supported by a great deal of evidence for the mechanism part.

It accepts the mechanisms above. It also holds that mechanisms answer “how did it come about,” and do not answer “why is the world so abundant, beyond any person’s need?” A God who delights in creating can naturally account for this surplus, but that is an inference, not an experimental result.

blocks.h: When He made it, He was not waiting for our applause
When the psalmist wrote this passage, all he saw was the sea from the shore. He already knew that the water went far beyond what he knew.

LORD, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches. There is the sea, great and wide, in which are innumerable living things, both small and large animals.
Genesis records God’s reaction after He made the living creatures of the waters. At that time there were no people on the earth, and the seats were empty.
God created the large sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, after their kind, and every winged bird after its kind. God saw that it was good.

This God who sees in dark places also sees you. Many of the most important things in life happen in places without lights: prayer late at night, forgiveness no one knows about, the thousandth time caring for a parent with dementia.
But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

Jesus Himself linked the deepest sea with His own death. Jonah spoke of being thrown into the deep, and Jesus said that the Son of Man would be the same. He did not stand on the shore throwing a life ring; He went down personally to the very depth of death, and on the third day rose and came up from there.
For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the huge fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
So what the prophet says has become even more certain because of the cross: the things you least dare to have fished up, God Himself has thrown into the depths of the sea.
He will again have compassion on us. He will tread our iniquities under foot. You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.

Tonight turn off the lights in your room and sit for one minute. In that darkness imagine that right now, in the water four thousand meters down, a small animal whose name you will never know has flashed once. No one saw it. God saw.
Meditate: Is there something I do that I would no longer want to do because no one sees it? If only God sees it, is that enough for me?

Pray: Lord who made the deep sea, Your riches far exceed what I know. Thank You for watching in secret, and for seeing my tears and struggles that no one knows. Thank You, Lord Jesus, for going down to the depths of death for me and rising again. Let me keep shining faithfully in places without applause. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Selflessness: deep-sea creatures do not live because humans look at them. My service too can set down the craving to be seen, and turn from “does anyone know?” to “God knows.”
Turn from the temporary to the eternal view: faithfulness that no one sees today is not wasted before God.

Letting God be God and people be people: humans have seen one hundred-thousandth of the seafloor, and my knowledge of God is just as limited. Honestly saying “I don’t know” is the beginning of humility.

blocks.h: This week: Quietly do one good thing for someone this week: pay a bill, tidy a corner, write out a prayer, with no name attached and without revealing it afterward.
Pass it on: If a good deed you did were never known by anyone, would it still have value in your opinion? Why?
Quick quiz

quiz.q: What does “less than 0.001%” refer to?
o: The share of the seafloor humans have mapped with sonar
The share of the deep seafloor humans have seen with their own eyes or with cameras
The share of known species in the deep sea
quiz.e: Sonar mapping covers about 28.7% (April 2026); it is the deep seafloor seen with eyes that is less than 0.001%.

quiz.q: What is the starting point of the food chain in the vent community discovered in 1977?
quiz.e: Bacteria use hydrogen sulfide to make nutrients, and the other animals live on them.

quiz.q: Which statement about “76% of animals glow” is most accurate?
o: It is established for the global ocean
It is true only below 3,000 meters
It is a statistic from off California, from the surface to about 3,900 meters
quiz.e: The figure comes from 17 years of footage off California; whether it can be extrapolated to the globe needs more data.

units.title: Forests: The Earth’s Lungs and Network
units.sub: Both “lungs of the Earth” and the “wood wide web” have been overstated. After checking the facts, forests turn out to be even more worthy of awe.

share.v: Then all the trees of the woods shall sing for joy

blocks.h: When the Amazon burned in 2019, one line was passed around the whole world: the Amazon produces 20% of the Earth’s oxygen. Presidents, senators and major media all said it. The claim is wrong.

Trees do release oxygen. They also use it themselves, and when fallen leaves and dead wood are broken down by microbes, even more is used up. By the calculation of Yadvinder Malhi, an ecologist at the University of Oxford, the Amazon’s net contribution to atmospheric oxygen is almost zero.
So do forests still matter? They matter far more, though for different reasons than the ones you were told.
God said, “Let the earth yield grass, herbs yielding seeds, and fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind, with their seeds in it, on the earth;” and it was so.
Correction one: the lungs of the Earth

Scientists think the 20% figure is overstated by at least a factor of two. The Amazon accounts for roughly 12–16% of photosynthesis on land, and the oceans account for about half of global photosynthesis, so its gross production is about 6–9% of the world’s oxygen. Subtract respiration and decomposition, and the net is close to zero. The oxygen in the atmosphere is an enormous stockpile built up over geological ages; even if every forest burned down, the oxygen concentration would fall only from 20.9% to about 20.4%.

A “lung” is actually an organ that consumes oxygen, so the metaphor is right by accident. A forest is more like the central air conditioning and water tower of a whole building: it absorbs carbon dioxide, releases water vapor and regulates rainfall. If it shut down, you would not suffocate at once, but the climate of the whole building would be thrown into chaos.
What forests really do
The 2025 assessment by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations puts the world’s forests at about 4.14 billion hectares, 32% of the land, storing about 714 gigatonnes of carbon.

Forests also make rain. A 2012 study of tropical satellite data found that rainfall rose markedly in regions where the air had first passed over forest. The Amazon is also regarded as the key to stabilizing rainfall across South America, and the scientist Michael Coe has compared it to the planet’s giant air conditioner.
Deforestation is slowing but has not stopped: 17.6 million hectares a year in the 1990s, and 10.9 million hectares a year in 2015–2025, roughly three Taiwans every year.
Correction two: the wood wide web

In 1997 the Canadian scholar Suzanne Simard and colleagues reported in Nature that, in the field, carbon could be transferred (net) between different tree species through mycorrhizal fungi. This opened up research on the “underground network,” and also led to the bestselling story that mother trees recognize their own children through a fungal web and pass nutrients and warnings to them.

In 2023 Justine Karst, Melanie Jones and Jason Hoeksema re-examined the evidence in Nature Ecology & Evolution. It is worth noting that Jones was herself a co-author of the 1997 paper. They found that only five studies had actually confirmed a network by genetic sequencing, involving two tree species; the results of 26 field studies all had other possible explanations; and no peer-reviewed field evidence was found that mother trees give their offspring priority. Moreover, papers citing these studies increasingly said more than the studies themselves did, with unsupported citations in the functional category approaching half.

items.h: Mycorrhizal links do exist, and there are measured data on carbon moving between trees. The forest is an interacting whole, a direction worth continuing to research, and one that has already changed how people see forests.

The links exist in a few cases, but how widespread, how lasting and how functionally significant they are remains unknown; current knowledge is too thin to guide forest management. In 2024 another group of plant scientists also warned that describing trees as mothers who care for their children is easily misleading.

blocks.h: An honest summary: the symbiosis of fungi and tree roots is established fact; “trees caring for one another through a fungal web” is a beautiful claim not yet confirmed.
That a field can have one of its original co-authors step forward and tap the brakes is itself one of the precious things about science: it is able to correct itself.

The long-term course of the forest carbon sink also has to be stated carefully. A 2024 global assessment in Nature used the word “enduring” for the world’s forest carbon sink, but regions differ greatly, and tropical deforestation is still offsetting many of the gains.
Let’s look at each claim separately and mark how certain it is.
The claim that the Amazon produces 20% of the world’s oxygen is incorrect; its net oxygen contribution is close to zero.

In 2025 the world’s forests covered about 4.14 billion hectares, 32% of the land; the rate of deforestation has fallen from 17.6 million hectares a year in the 1990s to 10.9 million hectares a year in 2015–2025.
Forests can increase rainfall downwind. Observations in the tropics support this; the strength varies from place to place and is still being refined.
Mycorrhizal networks are common in forests and significantly help seedlings. There are studies both supporting and questioning this, and the present evidence is not enough to settle it.
Mother trees give priority to their offspring through fungal networks. There is currently no peer-reviewed field evidence for this.

Forests quietly supply climate, rain and habitat far beyond what human design could achieve, which can reasonably lead us to thank the Creator. This is a faith interpretation; ecology does not declare it.
The trees He made delight us, and keep us alive
God’s first comment on trees puts them in the same sentence as the usefulness of their fruit: pleasant to look at, and good to eat. His goodness is not only about being practical.

Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
When the man was placed in this garden, he was handed two verbs.
Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
Even in the middle of a war, God speaks up for the trees. In an ancient book of law, this sentence comes as a surprise.

When you shall besiege a city a long time, in making war against it to take it, you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an ax against them; for you may eat of them. You shall not cut them down, for is the tree of the field man, that it should be besieged by you?

The Bible’s story begins with a tree and ends with a tree. In between stands the heaviest one of all, a cross made of wood. A hand reached out from a tree and brought death into the world; Christ was hung on wood and brought life back.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.
On this side of the river and on that was the tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruits, yielding its fruit every month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.

This week, find a tree, stand under it for three minutes and put your hand on the trunk. It is pushing water up from the ground and turning the carbon dioxide you breathed out into wood. It does not know you came by, and it serves just the same.
Reflect: Do I often feel I have to exaggerate something before it seems worth giving thanks for? Is what God really made enough for me?

Pray: Lord who made the trees, thank You for letting the forests regulate the climate and bring rain for me without my ever noticing. Thank You, Lord Jesus, for being hung on wood for me, and for rising again, and for giving me the hope of the tree of life. Help me to speak the truth, and to keep well the earth You have entrusted to us. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: Faith does not need exaggerated testimonies to hold up the show. Before you preach or share the gospel, check the facts first; that is also a way of loving God.
235 spiritual companions: Being connected to one another does not need fungi to prove it; it is the Lord’s command. Find a spiritual companion, reach out this week and ask how they are really doing.
Build God's kingdom system: Cultivating and keeping begin with small things. Waste less paper and wood, and leave a patch of shade for the next generation.

blocks.h: This week: Fact-check one “seems so moving” message you once forwarded, and correct it if it was wrong; then get to know one tree nearby and find out its name.
Pass it on: Is there a tree you remember from childhood, or a wood you used to visit? What did it make you feel?
Quiz

quiz.q: Why is “the Amazon produces 20% of the Earth’s oxygen” incorrect?
o: The Amazon does not actually carry out photosynthesis
Most of the oxygen the trees release is used up again by respiration and decomposition, so the net contribution is close to zero
quiz.e: Gross production is about 6–9% of the global total; subtract respiration and decomposition and the net is close to zero. The importance of forests lies in carbon, rainfall and biodiversity.

quiz.q: On the idea that “mother trees care for their offspring through fungal networks,” what did Karst and colleagues conclude in 2023?
o: It has been confirmed by many field experiments
There is no peer-reviewed field evidence for it
It has been proven completely impossible
quiz.e: They pointed out that no such field evidence currently exists, and also warned that citations often say too much; this is different from “proven impossible.”

quiz.q: What work did God give the man in Genesis 2:15?
quiz.e: What the man was entrusted with was care and keeping.

units.title: Natural Disasters: Why Would a Loving God Allow Earthquakes?
units.sub: Let’s not rush to answer. First, sit down and weep together. Only then can we talk honestly about what we know and what we don’t.

share.v: Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

blocks.h: If you or someone you love is in the pain of a disaster right now, please know this first: this page does not ask you to work anything out right away. You can skip straight to the prayer, you can stop here, and you can be angry with God. People in the Bible did all of these things.

At 1:47 a.m. on September 21, 1999, people in central Taiwan were shaken awake in their sleep. The earthquake took 2,415 lives, and 29 people were left missing. As a number, that is one line of type; to a family, it is a bed that no one will ever sleep in again.
Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
Sit down first

After Job lost his children, three friends rushed to him and did one thing right and one thing wrong. First they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights without saying a word, and that was right. Then they opened their mouths to explain, saying he must have done something wrong. By the end of the book, God says they spoke wrongly.
So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.

Modern research on disaster psychology points in the same direction. The World Health Organization’s 2011 Psychological First Aid guide reminds helpers to offer practical help, to listen, and not to pressure people to tell their story. Hobfoll and colleagues identified five elements of support after a disaster: safety, calm, a sense of efficacy, connection and hope.
Why does the ground shake?

The Earth’s crust is divided into plates that push against one another and slide beneath one another. The boundaries often stick, and stress slowly builds until the rock can hold no more and slips in an instant. That is an earthquake. If the seafloor moves greatly as a result, a tsunami can be raised.

Press a plastic ruler down at the edge of a table and let it bend slowly. When your finger slips, the ruler snaps back. A plate boundary works the same way, except that this ruler is hundreds of kilometers long and has been bending for hundreds of years.

On December 26, 2004, a magnitude 9.1 earthquake struck the subduction zone where the Indian plate dives beneath the sea off Sumatra. The tsunami reached 14 countries, and about 228,000 people died or went missing. On February 6, 2023, earthquakes of magnitude 7.8 and 7.7 struck one after the other on the border of Türkiye and Syria, killing more than 50,000 people in Türkiye and 5,954 in Syria.
Two honest things that are hard to hear

First, the same plate and volcanic activity that raises mountains and drives the carbon cycle is also linked to the Earth’s long-term stable climate. We write it here only because it is true. It has no right to offer comfort to parents searching the rubble for their child, and it is not enough to answer “why him?”

Second, casualties are not determined by nature alone. In 1756 Rousseau, responding to Voltaire’s poem on the Lisbon earthquake, pointed out that it was not nature that built twenty thousand houses of six or seven stories packed together. In 2011 Ambraseys and Bilham, in a commentary in Nature analyzing the previous 30 years, found that about 83% of earthquake deaths caused by collapsing buildings occurred in countries with relatively high levels of corruption. The authors also explain that corruption is hard to quantify directly and is closely tied to poverty. This points to responsibility in construction and oversight, and it shows that the poor bear the heaviest burden. It is in no way blaming the dead.

Figures vary greatly from year to year. According to preliminary statistics from the EM-DAT database of the Centre for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED) in Belgium, in 2024 there were 393 disasters related to natural hazards worldwide, with 16,753 deaths, below the 2004–2023 average of 65,566. The main reason was that the year had no giant disaster causing mass death; deaths from heat may be underestimated.
Some things are already clear, some are still being debated, and some we simply do not know. Let’s look at them separately.
Earthquakes occur mainly at plate boundaries and are caused by the sudden release of accumulated stress; tsunamis are mostly triggered by large undersea earthquakes.
For the 2004 Indian Ocean magnitude 9.1 earthquake and tsunami, the U.S. Geological Survey records 227,898 people dead or missing.

Earthquake deaths are strongly linked to building quality, poverty and governance. The 83% figure comes from a commentary article, and its corruption measure relies on the Corruption Perceptions Index.
Plate and volcanic processes take part in the Earth’s long-term carbon cycle and climate stability; but whether plate tectonics is a necessary condition for habitability has not been settled.

The Bible rejects the inference that “those struck by disaster must be greater sinners than others.” Why God allows any particular disaster, the Bible does not give an answer we can apply, and Christians should not announce one on God’s behalf.
Perspectives Room
This is one of the hardest questions for faith. The views below are set side by side without a verdict, and each has unresolved difficulties.

items.h: A God who is all-powerful and all-good should be able to make a world without tsunamis, or at least to stop one at that moment. Natural explanations are already sufficient, and adding God only adds difficulties. This question is serious, it comes from a real moral sense, and it should not be brushed aside.

The world is now in a state of being “subjected to vanity” (Romans 8:20-22). After the South Asian tsunami the theologian David Bentley Hart wrote The Doors of the Sea (2005), opposing the explanation of such disasters as a necessary part of God’s beautiful plan; Christian outrage itself has a basis. The difficulty: earthquakes are far older than humankind, and explanations differ on how the Fall affected the natural world.

items.n: The cost of a natural order
items.h: The physicist and theologian John Polkinghorne proposed the “free process defense”: God gave creation real autonomy, and a world that can form itself is better than a puppet theater. The difficulties: is this enough for the victims? Why does God not intervene?

The book of Job does not tell Job the reason; God simply speaks to him in person. D. A. Carson and others stress that both God’s sovereignty and His goodness must be held, and acknowledge a tension in this that humans cannot untie. The difficulty: this is easily turned into a cold “it is all God’s good will,” which is a misuse.

blocks.h: Jesus personally refuses that inference

Someone brought Jesus the news of a terrible tragedy, and He Himself added another, a building disaster of the time. His answer cuts straight through the logic of “they suffered, so they were guilty.”
Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem? I tell you, no
The words that follow, “unless you repent,” are spoken to the living questioners. He draws His finger back from the dead and turns it toward everyone who is still alive.
Creation groans

For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now. Not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.
The Bible does not describe this world as everything being fine. The word Paul uses is groaning.
God’s answer is a person
Standing before Lazarus’s tomb, Jesus knew perfectly well that He was about to raise him, and still He wept.
Jesus wept.

On the cross, He also cried out the most painful question humanity can ask. God did not hand us a report explaining disasters; He entered the suffering Himself, died, and rose again. The cross does not answer every “why”; it tells us that God is not watching from a distance. And the resurrection tells us that all of this will not have the last word.
About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.”
Think of a disaster you remember, or a loss of your own. Say a name or a place. You do not have to explain; speak to God in the way of the Psalms: How long?
Reflect: When others are suffering, do I tend to want to explain, or am I more willing to keep them company? Is there a question for God in my heart that I dare not say aloud?

Pray: Lord, how long? We do not understand. Draw near to those who are still waiting for news, still cleaning up their homes, still waking in the night. Lord Jesus, You wept and You cried out; be with them. Forgive us for the careless words we have spoken. Make us outstretched hands. May the day when You wipe away every tear come soon. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: People matter more than tasks: Presence comes before explanation. To people in pain, say less of “God’s good will,” “they must have done something,” and “God will not give you more than you can bear,” and more of “I’m here. What do you need?”
Jesus is my example: He wept first, then acted. Weep with those who weep, and then roll up your sleeves.
Build God's kingdom system: Preparing for disasters is also loving our neighbor. Church building safety, emergency contacts and a list of the vulnerable are all practical love.

blocks.h: Christians have a long history of reaching out in disasters. In the plague of the third century, a letter of Bishop Dionysius of Alexandria (preserved in Eusebius, Church History 7.22) records Christians caring for the sick, some of them dying as a result; scholars caution that these are Christians’ own accounts and may overlook the good deeds of others. After 921, the Christian Salvation Service also set up relief stations and supply depots. This is not a competition; other religions and civic groups were at the scene as well.

This week: With your family or small group, confirm one disaster-preparedness item: evacuation routes, an emergency kit, or how to reach the elderly. Then choose one verifiable relief organization with transparent finances, or pray for a disaster-stricken region.
Pass it on: When you see disaster in the news, what is the thing you most want to ask? If there is a God, what would you most want to ask Him?
Quiz

quiz.q: In Luke 13, what did Jesus say about those killed when the tower in Siloam fell?
o: They must have been worse sinners than others
They were not worse offenders than others
What happened to them was a punishment on the whole city
quiz.e: Jesus said plainly, “no,” and turned the warning toward everyone who is still alive.

quiz.q: Which of these is most appropriate when keeping company with someone who has just been through a disaster?
o: Make them tell the whole experience in order to heal
Offer practical help, listen, and do not pressure them to talk
quiz.e: This is the principle of psychological first aid, and it also fits the first seven days of Job’s friends’ company.

quiz.q: About the study behind “83% of building-collapse deaths,” which understanding is correct?
o: It points to responsibility in construction and oversight, and shows that the poor are hit hardest
It shows that the victims are responsible for their own deaths
It proves that earthquakes are a punishment for corruption
quiz.e: This is a problem of buildings and institutions, not the sin of the victims; the study also has limits in how it measures.
